name: Achilles Lock
description: Master the Achilles Lock leg submission in BJJ. Complete guide covering setup mechanics, finishing details, and safety protocols from Ashi Garami positions.
summary: The Achilles Lock is a straight-ankle leg lock that wedges the forearm or wrist bone across the Achilles tendon and extends the hips, compressing the tendon and hyperextending the ankle to force a tap from Ashi Garami positions.

disambiguations.name: Straight Ankle Lock
disambiguations.reason: the Straight Ankle Lock hyperextends the ankle joint rather than compressing the tendon

overview: The Achilles Lock is a fundamental leg lock submission that targets the Achilles tendon and ankle joint by creating hyperextension and compression. Unlike heel hooks which attack rotational integrity, the Achilles Lock applies straight pressure to the posterior ankle, making it one of the safer leg attacks when applied with control. This submission is legal at all IBJJF belt levels (with straight ankle variations) and serves as the foundation for understanding leg lock mechanics. The position is typically entered from Ashi Garami variations, Single Leg X-Guard, or during scrambles when controlling an opponent's leg. The effectiveness of the Achilles Lock depends on precise hip placement, proper grip configuration, and the ability to create a fulcrum against the opponent's Achilles tendon using your forearm or wrist bone. Understanding this submission is essential for developing a complete leg lock game and provides critical defensive awareness for all practitioners.

injury_risks.recovery_time: 6-12 months with surgery, potential permanent damage

safety_considerations.application_speed: SLOW and progressive - 3-5 seconds minimum from initial pressure to full extension. Never spike or jerk the submission.
tap_signals: Verbal tap (saying 'tap' or any distress signal)
Physical hand tap on partner or mat
Physical foot tap with free leg
Any unusual screaming or distress vocalization
Loss of resistance or going limp
release_protocol: Immediately release hip extension and return hips to mat
Maintain leg control but remove all pressure from ankle
Slowly open guard and release leg in controlled manner
Check with partner verbally before resuming training
Never release suddenly or drop the leg
training_restrictions: Never apply at competition speed during training
Always communicate with training partner about pressure levels
Stop immediately at any sign of discomfort
Beginners should only practice setup and positioning without pressure
Never combine with twisting or rotational pressure
Avoid training this submission if partner has existing ankle or Achilles injuries

variations.name: from Inside Ashi-Garami
variations.description: Primary Achilles Lock variant from inside leg entanglement with superior hip control

variations_and_setups.description: Instead of gable grip, use one arm to thread under the ankle and grab your own wrist/forearm creating a figure-four configuration. This provides more leverage and a sharper fulcrum point.
variations_and_setups.when_to_use: Use when opponent has strong ankle flexibility or when you need maximum breaking power. Also effective when transitioning from other leg attacks.

variations_and_setups.description: Instead of sitting back, turn your body face-down toward the mat while maintaining heel control. Use your body weight and chest pressure to drive the submission while extending hips.
variations_and_setups.when_to_use: Effective when opponent is successfully defending the standard version by sitting up. Also useful in no-gi when grips are harder to maintain.

variations_and_setups.description: From outside Ashi position (your outside leg over opponent's hip, inside leg under), the same mechanics apply but your body is positioned on the outside of their leg. Often provides better control against defensive hip rotation.
variations_and_setups.when_to_use: Use when opponent is defending standard Ashi by turning their knee inward. Outside position prevents this defense and provides different angle.

variations_and_setups.variation_name: Achilles Lock from Single Leg X Guard
variations_and_setups.description: From Single Leg X position, extend opponent's leg straight and transition your leg configuration to Ashi while maintaining heel control. The elevation makes the setup easier.
variations_and_setups.when_to_use: Natural transition during guard passing sequences or when opponent tries to pass your Single Leg X. The elevated position often surprises opponents.
